mission_08: Excellent work implementing a keyword spotting system! You now understand how to build lightweight, low-latency speech detection models suitable for always-on edge devices. The MFCC feature extraction provides a compact representation that captures the spectral characteristics of keywords while being computationally efficient. The DS-CNN architecture achieves a remarkable balance between accuracy and efficiency by using depthwise separable convolutions that reduce parameters by a factor of approximately the kernel size compared to standard convolutions. Batch normalization stabilizes training by normalizing activations, and ReLU introduces non-linearity while being computationally cheap. The sliding window detection approach enables continuous monitoring of the audio stream, classifying each window and collecting high-confidence detections. This architecture is directly applicable to wake word detection, voice command recognition, and other always-listening applications where power efficiency and low latency are critical constraints. The techniques you implemented form the foundation of keyword spotting systems deployed on billions of devices worldwide.
